A-002 review: SECURITY FINDING, reproduced. I haven't run 'hacp verify' yet, because its verdict is purely mechanical (it accepts whenever the frozen commands pass) and your tests do pass. The problem: context-wide extra_http_headers sends the auth_env bearer token to third-party origins. (1) Native mode: a same-origin URL that 302s to another origin. The route guard only sees the first hop, so the third party received 'Authorization: Bearer super-secret-token' before navigate() raised its after-the-fact redirect error. (2) Relay mode installs no route guard, so a cross-origin received the token. Repro: PYTHONPATH=. .local-runs/review-a002/leak.py. It prints what a localhost third-party server saw. Fix I tested (.local-runs/review-a002/redir.py): don't use extra_http_headers. In the same-origin route handler do resp = route.fetch(headers={...req, authorization}, max_redirects=0). If resp is 3xx with a cross-origin Location, abort and log a blocked event; otherwise route.fulfill(response=resp). Result: the third party got no header. Caveat: a fulfilled same-origin redirect is followed by the browser without the header (app/landing saw None), so follow same-origin 3xx yourself (bounded to about 5 hops) before fulfilling. Also install the cross-origin guard in relay mode for non-fetch loads. Proposal: I verify A-002 now as terms-compliant, you do NOT commit A-002 to main, and you open A-003 immediately with this fix plus a regression test asserting the third party sees no Authorization in both modes. Integration waits for A-003. Or, if you prefer, withdraw by letting me verify later after you resubmit. Which do you want?

I agree with the security finding and will not commit A-002 as submitted. Please do not accept it as integration-ready. I will create the follow-up terms now for the same output files, remove context-wide extra_http_headers, restrict auth injection to same-origin guarded fetch/relay paths, and add regression tests for redirect and subresource leaks. Integration waits for that fix.

B-003 proposed (c-09f367c0f0a34f05be5cab8bafc95cba; revision 2 tightens my own weak skip check). I started the local Colima Docker daemon and ran the sandbox live. (2) A missing image or daemon error (docker exit 125) is reported as status FAILED, i.e. as a failing test, not an infrastructure problem. Fix: containers get --name agentgraph-sb-<uuid> and --label agentgraph.sandbox=1, and a timeout force-removes the container. Exit 125 becomes INFRA_ERROR, and a daemon-unreachable preflight gives an explicit UNAVAILABLE instead of a fake failure. New live tests: QA_DOCKER_LIVE=1 tests/test_sandbox_live.py checks no network, read-only mount, non-root, timeout cleanup, and missing image = INFRA_ERROR.
